source_name: MNB — Közvetítők keresése (intermediaries register)
why_relevant: Register of money-market and insurance intermediaries/agents. Payment-service distribution partners and agent networks (including cash-in/cash-out and POS distribution agents) surface here rather than in the main institution register.

source_name: MNB — Határozatok és végzések keresése (supervisory decisions & rulings search)
why_relevant: Searchable full text of MNB licensing, enforcement, market-supervision and consumer-protection decisions, filterable by period, sector and type. New payment-institution licences, licence withdrawals, and sanctions appear here first — the earliest structured signal of market entry/exit and of compliance problems at PSPs.

source_name: MNB Aranykönyv (Golden Book) — per-institution supervisory data, interactive + xlsx
why_relevant: Institution-level balance sheet and income data for credit institutions, financial enterprises, e-money issuers and payment service providers, as a time series (reported coverage 2003 onwards) in interactive and xlsx form. The single best source for sizing and ranking individual HU banks and PSPs.

source_name: MNB Felügyeleti statisztikák (supervisory statistics hub, statisztika.mnb.hu)
why_relevant: Verified hub listing all supervisory statistics families: supervisory banking statistics (latest + archive), financial enterprises, intermediaries, capital market, insurance, pension funds, Golden Books. Gives the exact URL tree for automated harvesting of aggregate sector data.

source_name: MNB FinTech és Digitalizációs Jelentés (FinTech and Digitalisation Report)
why_relevant: Annual supervisory/analytical report on the digital maturity of HU banks, insurers and investment firms and on the domestic FinTech ecosystem; contains payment-digitalisation shares, AFR/qvik adoption and fraud-filtering data. Complements the Payment Systems Report on the technology/vendor side.

source_name: Hitelintézeti Szemle (Financial and Economic Review), MNB scientific journal
why_relevant: MNB's peer-reviewed journal; publishes empirical studies on Hungarian card payments, regional card-usage patterns, cash demand and interchange economics (e.g. Kajdi–Nemecskó on regional characteristics of card payments). Gives methodology and micro-level insight unavailable in the aggregate tables.

source_name: MNB Tanulmányok / MNB Occasional Papers (MT series)
why_relevant: MNB working/occasional paper series carrying payment-economics research such as the social cost of Hungarian payment methods (MT93) and interchange fees in card systems (MT96) — the reference studies for cash-vs-card cost analysis in Hungary.

source_name: MNB — Pénzforgalmi intézmények adatszolgáltatás (reporting obligations page)
why_relevant: Sets out what payment institutions must report to the MNB and on what forms/frequency. Reveals which datasets exist upstream (even when only aggregates are published) and therefore what can be requested or expected to appear in supervisory statistics — critical for planning data acquisition on POS/acquiring volumes.

source_name: MNB Kiadványi publikációs naptár (publication calendar)
why_relevant: Announced release dates for all MNB reports (Payment Systems Report, FinTech Report, Financial Stability Report, Annual Report). Lets the collection pipeline be scheduled rather than polled, and flags schedule changes.

source_name: EBA central register of payment and e-money institutions (PSD2) — Hungary/MNB slice
why_relevant: EU-level mirror of the MNB national register, fed by the MNB at least daily and downloadable in bulk machine-readable form. Far easier to automate than the MNB search UI, and it also captures inbound EEA passporting into Hungary that the national register does not present.

source_name: MNB Felügyeleti hírek / sajtóközlemények (supervisory news and press releases)
why_relevant: Announcement layer: new Aranykönyv releases, register changes, licence grants/withdrawals, notification obligations for specific cash-substitute instrument issuers. A cheap high-frequency change-detection feed pointing at the heavier register and statistics sources.

source_name: Net Jogtár — 2013. évi CCXXXV. törvény az egyes fizetési szolgáltatókról (Fsztv.)
why_relevant: The statute that creates the payment-institution and e-money-institution categories and the MNB's registration duty. Defines the legal vocabulary used by every MNB register entry and states what must be published — the legal backbone for judging register completeness.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — Bank rovat (banking/payments desk)
why_relevant: Hungary's leading business/financial news portal. Its Bank desk systematically works up MNB payment statistics (pénzforgalmi adatok, Fizetési rendszer jelentés) into charted analyses within hours of release, and frequently obtains vendor/bank figures via interviews before formal publication. Observed 2026 articles cover ATM cash withdrawal behaviour after the free-withdrawal limit rise, payment-mix shifts, qvik growth multiples, PSP revenue (HUF 274bn) and card fraud values.

source_name: Pénzcentrum
why_relevant: High-volume consumer-finance portal that repackages MNB/bank data on cash usage, ATM fees and limits, free-cash-withdrawal rules, and account/card penetration. Useful as an early-warning and consumer-behaviour layer, and its /megtakaritas section carries recurring bank-by-bank ATM limit and fee comparisons that are not published centrally.

source_name: FinTechZone.hu
why_relevant: The specialist Hungarian fintech/payments trade outlet. Publishes quantified qvik and instant-payment analyses (transaction counts, HUF volumes, share of instant transfers by quarter) and vendor interviews (e.g. SimplePay) that surface acquirer-level data available nowhere else. Also runs a topical taxonomy (/kategoria/elektronikus-fizetes/azonnali-fizetes/, /tag/qvik/) that acts as a pointer index to Hungarian payment actors.

source_name: FinTechZone — Elektronikus fizetési megoldások kézikönyve
why_relevant: A standing handbook/directory of electronic payment solutions available in Hungary. Functions as an actor map: PSPs, acquirers, wallet and instant-payment providers with descriptions — an efficient way to snowball into vendor-level primary sources for the HU payments market.

source_name: Bank360.hu — bank product comparison and calculators
why_relevant: Comparison portal that maintains a structured, continuously updated database of Hungarian current-account, debit/credit card and student-account offers including per-transaction fees (számlavezetési díj, készpénzfelvételi díj, kártyadíj). This fee-level market data is compiled from bank hirdetmény documents and exists in aggregated form essentially nowhere else — a direct dataset for pricing/market-structure work.

source_name: Bankmonitor.hu
why_relevant: Comparison site plus an editorial 'médiatár' that publishes its own derived market analyses — e.g. comparing 58 current-account offers and quantifying the spread in two-year card costs. Both the underlying product database and the derived analyses are usable market-structure and pricing intelligence.

source_name: Bonline.hu (Világgazdaság / VG media group business portal)
why_relevant: Carries granular acquiring-infrastructure analysis: observed article reports the first-ever decline in physical card-accepting locations (154,821 at end-September vs a 159,270 peak at end-2023, -4,449 / ~3%), alongside 65,806 card-accepting webshops (+15% y/y) and card purchase growth of 4-5% in count and 9-10% in value. Exactly the ATM/POS and card-statistics granularity this cell targets.

source_name: Világgazdaság (vg.hu)
why_relevant: Long-running Hungarian business daily, same media group as bonline.hu; standard destination for MNB payment-report coverage and bank-sector reporting. Included in the cell brief; searches surfaced the group's bonline.hu output rather than vg.hu article URLs directly, so its payments-specific yield is asserted at lower confidence.

source_name: Napi.hu
why_relevant: Named in the cell brief as a mainstream Hungarian business/finance portal that covers MNB payment and cash-withdrawal statistics. Two targeted hu-language searches returned no napi.hu article URLs, so relevance is inferred from its general remit rather than observed payments output — track at lower priority until article-level coverage is confirmed.

source_name: Forbes.hu — Pénz / Üzlet rovat
why_relevant: Runs investigative and exclusive fintech/banking reporting rather than statistics rewrites: observed exclusives on Revolut's Hungarian branch licensing and customer base, bank fraud-refund practices, and funding rounds for Hungarian fintechs (SEON, Salarify). Best source in the cell for competitive/market-entry intelligence and for figures obtained by interview.

source_name: Fintech.hu
why_relevant: Second specialist Hungarian fintech outlet (distinct from FinTechZone). Observed a forward-looking analysis of what changes in Hungarian payment acceptance in 2026 and what SMEs stand to gain — merchant-side acquiring economics, SoftPOS, bank-independent acquirers. Adds acceptance-side coverage that the mainstream portals treat thinly.

source_name: HVG / hvg360 — POS terminál and payments coverage
why_relevant: Major weekly/news group with a maintained 'POS terminál' tag page acting as a ready-made topical archive, and hvg360 long-form that syndicates or parallels specialist acceptance analyses. The tag page itself is a pointer index into HU acquiring coverage over time.

source_name: Mfor.hu (Menedzsment Fórum)
why_relevant: Business/management outlet covering merchant-side payment mechanics (e.g. settlement timing of card payments to merchants) — operational acquiring detail that rarely appears in statistical releases and is directly relevant to POS/acceptance market analysis.

source_name: Danube Capital — blog: POS terminálok száma Magyarországon
why_relevant: Analyst/advisory firm blog that appears to compile and time-series the Hungarian POS terminal count. Analyst blogs of this kind often present tidier long-run series than the raw MNB tables and reveal the compiler's methodology; valuable both as a data pointer and as a competitor-analysis artefact.

source_name: Biztosdöntés.hu
why_relevant: Comparison/advice portal publishing analytical pieces that pair ATM-count records with declining cash-withdrawal volumes, and track the 2026 free-cash-withdrawal rule changes. Complements Bankmonitor/Bank360 as a third compiler of HU retail banking fee and ATM-network facts.
